model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: No SBC in the employee sense (externally managed). The SBC-equivalent is the Manager's base and performance fees paid/payable in Units: S$3.225m + S$2.337m = S$5.562m FY2026 (FY2026 AR Distribution Statements Note A, O5RU.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:10810-10813). Distributable income adds these back as non-cash, so the house basis deducts them and holds the unit count flat; the street basis (distributions as declared) does not.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T09:04:17Z (17:04 SGT, after the SGX 17:00 close -- the regular close of 23 Oct 2026)
inputs.share_count_basis: Units in issue and to be issued at 31 March 2026, 820.561m (FY2026 AR note 17, O5RU.SI_Annual_FY2026.txt:13810), including fee units to be issued. Held FLAT because Manager fees paid in Units are charged in the flow (sbc_pct_path). The 1Q FY2027 distribution of S$19.3m at 2.337c implies ~826m units entitled (rounding band 824-828m); not booked because the 1Q FY2027 update is not in the extracted filings -- if confirmed it lowers every per-unit value ~0.6%.
inputs.affo_build: Flow capitalised = AFFO to Unitholders = distributable income to Unitholders (after property expenses, land rent, Manager cash fees, trust expenses, interest and the amount reserved for Perpetual Securities holders) - Manager fees paid in Units - maintenance capex. Engine mapping: revenue = gross revenue; ebitda_margin_path = distributions to Unitholders / gross revenue (FY2026: 80.613 / 190.665 = 42.3%); sbc_pct_path = fees paid in Units / gross revenue (2.9%); capex_pct_path = maintenance capex / gross revenue; D&A, lease charge and cash tax are 0 because distributable income is already after land rent (Note A nets land rent paid against FRS116 interest) and the trust is tax-transparent on distributed Singapore taxable income. FY2026 AFFO = 80.6 - 5.6 - ~6.7 (3.5% maintenance capex) = ~68.3m, ~8.3c/unit vs DPU 9.85c.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026 AFFO-equivalent on the house basis, rounded: distributions 80.6 - fee units 5.6 = 75.0 before maintenance capex (the engine charges capex from capex_pct_path). reported_fcf is OCF less capex from the cash flow statement and is NOT the valued flow (it is pre-interest, pre-perpetual distributions).
inputs.wacc_rationale: This is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC: the flow is after interest and after perpetual-securities distributions, so it is capitalised at the unitholder rate and net debt is held at 0 (deducting it would charge the debt twice). SGD-built: Singapore 10-year SGS ~2.3%, equity risk premium 5.5%, S-REIT beta ~0.85 (4.7%), plus ~1.0pp for sub-scale, external-manager and perpetual-securities subordination = ~8.0% base. Bull 7.5% (index inclusion / scale), bear 9.0% (refinancing at higher rates, governance discount after CEO change).
inputs.lease_treatment: Single treatment: land rent paid (S$9.1m FY2026) is already deducted inside distributable income (FY2026 AR Note A: land rent paid -9.144, interest on lease liabilities +4.528). lease_cost_pct_path is 0 and lease liabilities (S$124.1m) are NOT added to debt -- doing either would charge the JTC land rent twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material NCI. Optus Centre is a 49% joint venture equity-accounted; distributable income includes AA REIT's share of JV distributions only.
inputs.perpetual_treatment: Perpetual securities (S$621.2m at 31 Mar 2026, of which S$250m 5.375% was redeemed Sep 2026, leaving ~S$375m at a blended ~4.3%) rank ahead of Unitholders. Their distributions are deducted inside the flow (amount reserved for Perpetual Securities holders S$23.4m FY2026), so their principal is NOT deducted again from the capitalised value. Unitholders' funds (S$1,046.2m, NAV S$1.28/unit) exclude them; total equity incl. perps is S$1,667.5m (kpis TotalEquityInclHybridNCI).
inputs.anchors: FY2026 (31 Mar 2026): gross revenue S$190.7m, NPI S$141.3m, distributions to Unitholders S$80.6m, DPU 9.850c, NAV S$1.28/unit, aggregate leverage 26.8% (24.9% at 1Q FY2027), interest cover 2.7x, occupancy 93.6% (96.1% at 1Q FY2027), WALE 4.0 years, gross borrowings S$570.2m, cash S$53.2m. 1Q FY2027 (Jun 2026): DPU 2.337c (+2.5% YoY), NPI +12.5%.
inputs.notes: Model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine with net_debt = 0 (dcf-methods routing row 'REIT / property trust (IAS 40 fair-value, external manager)'). AA REIT is an externally managed S-REIT carrying investment properties at fair value and paying out 100% of Singapore taxable income, so reported net income is revaluation noise (FY2026 S$107.8m includes a S$41.4m revaluation gain) and owner-FCF/EBITDA less net debt would double-charge interest and ignore the perpetual securities. First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY entry. NAV/unit (S$1.28) is the cross-check: price 1.40 is 1.09x NAV and a 7.0% DPU yield. Model check: total_debt and cash are recorded for reference only; net_debt is 0 by design.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Unitholders' equity CAGR (1.7%) is far below revenue CAGR (9.2% 5yr). Expected for this REIT: the FY2021-22 growth (Woolworths HQ, Boardriders) was funded partly with perpetual securities that sit outside unitholders' funds, units grew 3.0%/yr (706.7m -> 820.6m), and FY2024-25 revaluation losses cut NAV/unit from 1.40 to 1.23. Per-unit growth (DPU 1.9%/yr) is the relevant rate, not aggregate revenue.
historical_growth.notes: EPS and reported FCF CAGRs are not meaningful for a REIT (EPS is dominated by fair-value movements; reported FCF is pre-interest and pre-perpetual distributions). SBC (fee units) is a flat ~3% of revenue, so the house/street gap is stable rather than widening. Aggregate distributable income grew 5.0%/yr over 5 years but DPU only 1.9%/yr: most of the growth was paid for with new units and perpetual securities.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2027 +3%: full year of 2 Aljunied Ave 1 (Nov 2025) and ~7 months of Hazelmere (A$42.7m at ~5.3% NPI yield), occupancy recovery 93.6% -> 96.1% at 1Q, less 3 Toh Tuck Link and 8 Senoko South Road divested and the Optus partial vacancy at Macquarie Park. Then 2.5-3% from 2.0-3.25% fixed escalations plus positive Singapore reversions, fading to 2% as the rental upcycle matures and 2026-27 supply lands.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: Distributions/gross revenue 42.3% FY2026. FY2027 43.0% and FY2028 43.5% capture the ~S$3m guided perpetual refinancing saving (S$250m 5.375% redeemed Sep 2026, so half in FY2027, full in FY2028) and lower floating cost on the ~20% unhedged debt. Eased back to 43.0% from FY2031 for the 2030-31 perpetual resets and refinancing the 2.2-year debt book at normalised rates.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: Maintenance capex 3.5% of revenue (~S$6.7m). Total capex FY2021-24 ran 1.7-6.2% of revenue (S$3-7m) excluding AEI years; FY2025 (13.6%) and FY2026 (7.5%) were AEI-heavy (7 Clementi Loop, 15 Tai Seng). AEIs are growth capex funded off-balance of distributions, but a multi-tenanted industrial portfolio with ageing Singapore stock and 30-60-year JTC leases needs a real recurring charge; distributable income deducts none.
base.terminal_growth_rationale: 1.5%: below SGD inflation because a 100%-payout trust cannot fund growth internally and leasehold JTC land amortises toward zero; escalations net of obsolescence.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_rationale: 16x AFFO (6.25% AFFO yield) -- just above the Gordon multiple at 8%/1.5% (15.6x) so Gordon binds.

scenario_narratives.base: Income growth intact, capital discipline holds. Occupancy recovers toward 96% as the 1Q FY2027 print suggests, the perpetual refinancing delivers its ~S$3m saving, and 2-3.25% fixed escalations plus moderating Singapore reversions grow gross revenue 2.5-3% a year before fading to 2% as the 2026-27 industrial supply wave lands. The Optus partial vacancy at Macquarie Park is backfilled slowly. No transformational deals; small bolt-ons funded by capital recycling at roughly neutral accretion. AFFO per unit grows ~2.5% a year, close to the 1.9% DPU record, and the trust is worth a modest premium to NAV.
scenario_narratives.bull: The low-gearing balance sheet (24.9%) is put to work accretively: Hazelmere-style Australian industrial and Singapore logistics acquisitions plus the ~600k sqft Singapore / ~1.5m sqft Australian plot-ratio redevelopment pipeline lift revenue 4-4.5% a year, the NSW-endorsed data-centre optionality at Macquarie Park / Bella Vista starts to crystallise, reversions stay high-single-digit through the cycle, and scale earns a lower cost of equity (7.5%). AFFO margin widens to 44.5% as fixed-rate debt and cheaper perpetuals roll through.
scenario_narratives.bear: Anchor and supply risk together. Optus vacates more of Building A and Woolworths' HQ lease becomes a renewal question late in the decade; the 1.15m sqm 2026 and 1.88m sqm 2027 Singapore supply wave turns reversions flat-to-negative; occupancy slips back to ~93%. With a 2.2-year debt maturity and perpetual resets in 2030-31, refinancing at higher rates squeezes the AFFO margin to 40.5%, while ageing leasehold Singapore stock needs more capex (4.5%). The CEO/CFO transition coincides with a deal or two bought at thin spreads. Revenue is flat to +1.5%, and the market prices the trust at a sub-scale, externally managed discount (9% cost of equity).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: two tenants are ~22% of GRI with Optus already partly vacating, the CEO and CFO are both changing in late 2026, and a 2.2-year debt maturity plus S$375m of resettable perpetuals make the downside a financing-cost story that is genuinely live. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right (accretive deployment, redevelopment approvals, data-centre conversion, sustained reversions). Base holds 50% on a defensive 82.5%-essential-sector tenant base and the lowest gearing among peers.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A REIT is worth the AFFO it can distribute per unit, capitalised at what unitholders demand. For AA REIT that means distributions after interest and after perpetual-securities distributions, less the Manager fees it pays in new units (a real dilution cost the headline DPU excludes) and less a recurring maintenance capex charge distributable income never deducts. Net debt is not subtracted because the flow is already after financing. NAV/unit (S$1.28) is the cross-check; fair value should land within a modest band of it for a REIT earning near its cost of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Tenant concentration: Woolworths (12.4% of GRI) and Optus (9.7%); Optus has partly vacated Building A at Macquarie Park.
Perpetual securities (~S$375m after the Sep 2026 redemption) rank ahead of Unitholders and reset in 2030-31; a reset at higher rates comes straight out of AFFO.
Short 2.2-year weighted debt maturity and ~20% floating-rate debt: every 25bp is ~0.06c of DPU.
Singapore industrial supply rising to ~1.15m sqm (2026) and ~1.88m sqm (2027) against a maturing rental upcycle.
Leadership transition: CEO changed 1 Oct 2026, new CFO due end-December 2026, just as deployment accelerates.
Leasehold JTC land amortises; terminal growth above inflation would overstate a wasting-asset portfolio.
Unit count may be ~0.6% higher than the 31 Mar 2026 figure used (1Q FY2027 distribution implies ~826m units).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close, SGX); 52-week range 1.36-1.67.
data_sources.financials: AIMS APAC REIT Annual Reports FY2016-FY2026 (Distribution Statements, Note A tax adjustments, note 17 units in issue, perpetual securities note) and half-year/quarterly updates through H1 FY2026, via O5RU.SI_Metrics.csv and the kpis table (DistributableIncome, NAVPerShare, Gearing, Occupancy, WALE, InterestCoverageRatio).
data_sources.qualitative: O5RU.SI_Analysis.json (2026-10-24), including 1Q FY2027 results (Aug 2026), Hazelmere acquisition, perpetual refinancing guidance and the October 2026 management change.
